identity.title: Classic but Everlasting: Traditional Gradient-Based Algorithms Converges Fast Even in Time-Varying Multi-Player Games

problem.claim: Determine last-iterate convergence behavior and rates for EG and OG in constrained, time-varying multi-player games.

gap.claim: Existing results largely assume time-invariant payoffs; limited time-varying analyses focus on two-player bilinear zero-sum or strictly monotone games, leaving EG/OG behavior in other settings—especially multi-player convergence rates—understudied.

contributions.claim: Analyzes EG and OG on convergent perturbed games, using tangent residuals or modifications as a game potential and Nash-equilibrium proximity measure.

Proves an O(1/√T) last-iterate convergence rate on bounded convex closed sets when the perturbed games approach monotone games sufficiently quickly, with the result also holding for certain unconstrained perturbed games.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper addresses the open question of last-iterate convergence rates for EG and OG in constrained and time-varying settings.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report proving O(1/√T) last-iterate convergence rates for EG and OG under the stated perturbed-game conditions.
The authors report that these rates are similar to known tight results for corresponding time-invariant games.

narrative_sequence.summary: Prior last-iterate convergence analyses commonly rely on time-invariant game payoffs.
Time-varying results are limited, and EG/OG rates in broader settings—particularly multi-player games—remain insufficiently studied.
The paper studies EG and OG in convergent perturbed games using tangent residual-based measures and derives O(1/√T) rates under sufficiently fast convergence toward monotonicity.
The authors relate the resulting rates to known tight rates in analogous time-invariant games.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a broader time-varying model—perturbed games—to a structural condition, namely sufficiently fast convergence toward monotone games, before stating its rate guarantee.

lessons.interpretation: A useful theory-paper pattern is to express a difficult general setting through an explicit path-to-structure assumption, making the scope of the result legible.
lessons.application: When extending an algorithmic theorem to dynamic environments, state the limiting structural class and quantify the required approach rate before presenting the convergence bound.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when no meaningful limiting structure exists or when the dynamics cannot be summarized by a single convergence-to-class condition.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify what “fast enough” means, the precise perturbed-game assumptions, or the constants and interpretation of the last-iterate rate.
The particular unconstrained perturbed games covered by the result are not identified.
